advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the guard's `print` sink detection stderr-aware: skip a `print(...)` whose `file=` keyword is not stdout, so a stderr diagnostic is not falsely flagged.
evidence: scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py:128: `if _callee_name(node.func) in _STDOUT_SINKS:` then `for arg in node.args:` — the `file=` keyword is never consulted
Docstring intent at scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py:17-18 scopes flagging to stdout: "written to stdout — print(<X>), sys.stdout.write(<X>)"
verify_authorship.py:601 and dozens of other in-scope sites use `print(..., file=sys.stderr)`, so `print(json.dumps(x), file=sys.stderr)` is a realistic future shape the guard would misclassify
advisory.finding: The AST guard treats any `print(...)` call as a stdout sink by inspecting only node.args, ignoring the `file=` keyword. A future `print(json.dumps(diag), file=sys.stderr)` — a stderr diagnostic the guard's own docstring says is allowed — would be falsely reported as a stdout write, and only a spurious `# js-safe-ok:` sanction could clear it.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _Visitor.visit_Call, when the callee is `print`, inspect node.keywords for a `file=` argument and skip the call when it targets a non-stdout stream (e.g. sys.stderr).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the guard docstring's 'LLM-eval tooling out of scope' claim with the fact that src/rebar/_cli (which contains _llm_eval_commands.py) is a scan root.
evidence: scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py:26-27: "the reconciler daemon and the LLM-eval tooling are DIFFERENT contracts and out of scope"
The diff converts _llm_eval_commands.py's four emitters to js_safe_dumps, i.e. the guard does police it
advisory.finding: The guard docstring declares 'the LLM-eval tooling ... [is] out of scope', but src/rebar/_cli/_llm_eval_commands.py sits under the scanned root src/rebar/_cli and is converted to js_safe_dumps in this same change, so the scan actually covers it. The docstring's scope statement contradicts both SCAN_ROOTS and the diff.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs main()/the script over a synthetic --root containing `print(json.dumps(doc))` and asserts the exit code is 1 (and the violation is reported on stderr).
evidence: scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py:244 `if violations or bare_findings:` / `return 1` — the gate-failing behavior make lint depends on
tests/unit/test_cli_json_js_safe_guard.py:172 `assert completed.returncode == 0, completed.stderr` — the ONLY exit-code assertion, and it is on the clean path
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `main(` in the test file returns (no matches); no test drives main() over a tree containing a violation and asserts returncode==1
Named violating input: a scanned file containing `print(json.dumps(doc))` must cause main() to return 1
advisory.finding: The gate's exit-code-1-on-violation contract is untested: no test asserts main() (or the subprocess) returns a non-zero exit code when a real raw-json.dumps stdout sink exists. Only the clean path (returncode==0) is asserted in test_the_repository_is_clean. Since make lint relies on the non-zero exit to fail the build, a regression that made main() always return 0 (e.g. inverting the `if violations or bare_findings:` branch at line 244) would leave every test green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `def test_main_returns_1_on_violation(tmp_path): src=tmp_path/'src'/'rebar'/'_cli'; src.mkdir(parents=True); (src/'x.py').write_text('import json\nprint(json.dumps(doc))\n'); assert gate.main(['--root', str(tmp_path)]) == 1`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that places `print(json.dumps(doc))` under an out-of-scope path (e.g. src/rebar/_logging/) and asserts find_violations returns no violations for it.
evidence: scripts/check_cli_json_js_safe.py:59-64 SCAN_ROOTS defines the in-scope surface; docstring lines 24-27 declare _logging / reconciler / llm-eval out of scope
tests/unit/test_cli_json_js_safe_guard.py:32-34 `_scan` always writes into `src/rebar/_cli`, never an out-of-scope path
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `SCAN_ROOTS` in the test file returns (no matches)
Named input: `print(json.dumps(doc))` under `src/rebar/_logging/foo.py` should NOT be reported
advisory.finding: The SCAN_ROOTS scoping contract — that out-of-scope streams (rebar._logging, the reconciler daemon, LLM-eval tooling) are NOT scanned — is documented but has no negative test. No test places a `print(json.dumps(...))` in an out-of-scope directory and asserts it is not flagged, so an accidental widening (or narrowing) of SCAN_ROOTS / _iter_files would go undetected.
